fields.meta_description: Accounts payable automation from a prompt: invoice capture, PO matching, approval routing, payment runs, and a ledger you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Accounts Payable Automation That Fits Your Approval Rules
fields.hero_description: Describe how invoices arrive, who approves them, and when they get paid. Emergent builds the intake, matching, routing, payment runs, and a ledger you own.
fields.features_subheading: Accounts payable automation takes an invoice from inbox to paid without retyping it. Every step lives in one app you own.
fields.feature_1:
Invoice capture from email and uploads

Invoices that arrive by email, upload, or vendor portal are read into fields: vendor, number, dates, line items, and totals. Low-confidence fields wait for a person to check.
fields.feature_2:
Two-way and three-way matching

Each invoice is checked against its purchase order and goods receipt. Price, quantity, and total mismatches are held with the difference shown before anyone approves.
fields.feature_3:
Approval routing by amount and vendor

Bills route by amount, vendor, entity, or GL code to the right approver, with a Slack or email request, reminders on a timer, and escalation when a deadline is missed.
fields.feature_4:
Payment runs on your schedule

Approved bills are batched into weekly or early-pay runs and sent through the bank file or payments API you connect, so cash leaves on the dates you choose and not before.
fields.feature_5:
Posted to your accounting system

Bills, approvals, and payments sync to QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite through their APIs, coded to the right accounts, so the ledger matches the bank without rekeying.
fields.feature_6:
Rules and data you can take with you

The intake form, matching rules, approval chain, and ledger export to your GitHub repository as code. Change a rule by prompting, or hand the repo to your engineers.

fields.usecase_heading: AP Automation Workflows You Can Build Today
fields.tab_content_1:
Match every invoice to its PO before it reaches an approver

Accounts payable invoice automation for teams that buy against purchase orders. Each invoice is read, matched to the PO and the goods receipt, and held with the variance shown when price or quantity is off. Clean matches go straight to approval and post to your ERP.
fields.tab_content_2:
Pay recurring bills on time without a reminder spreadsheet

Software subscriptions, rent, and utilities arrive as recurring bills. The workflow checks each one against the expected amount, flags anything that jumped, routes increases for approval, and adds the rest to the next scheduled payment run.
fields.tab_content_3:
Route each entity's bills to its own controller

For groups running several entities, every invoice is tagged to the right company, routed to that entity's approver, and paid from the right bank account. One ledger shows spend by entity, vendor, and month, ready for the close.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pay contractors once their paperwork is complete

Contractors submit invoices from a phone, with W-9 and bank details collected once and checked on every submission. Approved invoices join the next payout run, and the records stay ready for 1099 season.

fields.howto_description: Map how invoices arrive, who approves what, and when you pay. The intake, matching, routing, and payment runs follow from those rules, in seven steps from inbox to paid.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Map how invoices reach you today
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the approval rules in plain English
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every way invoices arrive: a shared AP inbox, vendor portals, paper scans, and contractor emails. Note who touches each one and where it waits. That map becomes the intake and the routing, so nothing arrives outside the workflow.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the policy the way your controller would: who approves by amount, which vendors need procurement, what happens on entity-specific spend. Emergent turns those sentences into routing rules you can read and change later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose two-way or three-way matching per vendor type, and set the variance you accept on price and quantity. Anything outside the tolerance is held with the difference shown, so approvers only see invoices that need a decision.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, or your ERP so vendors, GL codes, and purchase orders sync in, and approved bills sync out. Coding suggestions come from your own history, and every posted bill links back to its source invoice.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick your payment days, early-pay rules for vendors that offer discounts, and the bank file or payments API that releases the money. Approved bills wait for the next run, so cash leaves on a schedule finance controls.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run a month of real invoices through the workflow before go-live. Compare the matches, routes, and coding against what your team did by hand, fix any rule that disagrees by prompting, and run the sample again until it agrees.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live and watch cycle time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Switch the AP inbox over, keep the old process as a fallback for one cycle, and track invoice-to-payment time and exception rate on the dashboard. Tighten the rules as patterns show up, with every change versioned in your repo.
